answer: Custody is bound to one serial history per identity, and the release schedule rewards depth of a single chain rather than the number of chains, so splitting a chain into siblings destroys the compounding the schedule was meant to reward. The cost of one more head is paid in full and is never amortised across the fleet. The hollow is the serial tenure, the ocean the custody window that must elapse, and the harbor the standing released at the end of it; the hollow is personal, the ocean is not skippable, and the harbor cannot be inherited by a sibling.
